brief.headline: Push for ₹290/KG to close the ₹3.91 L/yr gap we already pay to Shrinath — their weak finances (loss-making, 2/10 health) mean we need a second source now.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹290/KG on the main laminates (currently ₹295/KG)
priceAsk.basis: Shrinath Roto Pack already gives us ₹290/KG for the same ORS sachets; market band ₹205–305/kg confirms our current price sits at the top of what's fair, so closing the 1.7% gap to ₹290 is fully justified

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt — do not extend to them

brief.financialLeverage: They lost ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25 and score 2/10 on money health — very weak. We are 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so losing us won't break them, but their fragility (credit rating IVR BBB- / Stable, 2.15x debt, severe legal case(s), EPF and GST delays) means we cannot rely on them alone. Lead with securing supply by qualifying a second source, then use that risk to anchor the price ask at the ₹290/KG we already pay elsewhere — this keeps the conversation about fairness and supply security, not a squeeze that tips a fragile supplier over.

evidence.point: We pay ₹295/KG; Shrinath charges ₹290/KG for identical ORS laminates — a 1.7% gap
Closing that gap across all laminates saves us ₹3.91 L/yr
They made a loss in FY2024-25
Their money-health score is 2 out of 10 — distress zone (Altman Z 1.68, grey)
They owe 2.15 times their own cash and struggle to cover interest (0.06x)
Our ₹2.31 Cr spend is 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue — small but not tiny

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (already a tiny FDC supplier) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant — both film substrate AND conversion; can second-source at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter — pharma blister/sachet laminates; strong second-source (health D 31/100, revenue ₹222.04 Cr)

risks: They are loss-making (₹-23.68 Cr), carry severe legal cases, EPF and GST delays, and sit in the grey distress zone (1.68) — pushing too hard could tip them over and leave us scrambling for supply mid-season
Credit rating IVR BBB- / Stable and 2/10 money-health score mean they are not a supplier to lean on alone — start qualifying Huhtamaki or UFLEX now so we have a fallback before the next tender
Market ask shows ₹205–305/kg is the fair band and we sit at ₹295 (top end) — so the ₹290 ask is defensible, but if they refuse we have little room below that without shifting to a maker direct

We are only 0.33% of their revenue — losing us won't save them, so don't bluff a walk-away you can't execute; frame the ₹290 ask as aligning to the price we already pay Shrinath, not a take-it-or-leave-it ultimatum
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹295 when Shrinath gives us ₹290 for the same sachets — and with your recent financials we need to line up a second source anyway, so let's talk about closing that gap and keeping the volumes with you.
